newsitem.title: GERMANY: Degussa says can stretch platinum cover.
newsitem.headline: Degussa says can stretch platinum cover.

text.p: German catalytic converter manufacturer Degussa AG can handle the current supply tightness on the platinum market without cutting production, a trading department source at the Frankfurt-based company said.
"We have taken internal measures to ensure we won't face any raw materials shortages which could negatively affect our converter production," he said.
Major supplier Russia failed to resume long-delayed platinum and palladium shipments on Friday, which export officials had said might see the start of the 1997 campaign.
Degussa on June 6 warned it might curb production if shipments were suspended for another three or four weeks.
But the source said platinum supply had not been completely suspended and Degussa had been able to make small purchases to extend its cover, albeit at high prices.
Russia was in line to resume exports to Japan in July but the size of likely volumes was not known, he added.
Degussa produces between 15 and 25 percent of the world's catalytic converters, which filter harmful gases from car exhausts.
Platinum prices were calm, having soared earlier this month to a seven-year high when Russia's absence squeezed supply. -Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
